guide.summary: OpenProject documents an OAuth authorization code flow. The app is registered in each OpenProject instance's administration area, with the api_v3 scope selected, and the token is sent as a Bearer header. The read uses GET /api/v3/work_packages with offset and pageSize, following nextByOffset links. api_v3 is the standard API scope, and no read-only scope is documented, so the token's effective boundary is the standard API plus the connected user's permissions. Execution is untested. Distribution and review requirements for other customer organizations are not in the supplied sources.

findings.title: Authorization code flow is documented
findings.detail: The authorization URL takes response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope and prompt=consent. The code is exchanged at the token endpoint, which returns an access_token and expires_in.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
--url 'https://example.com/oauth/token' \ --header 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
"expires_in" : 7200 ,

findings.title: Request the api_v3 scope for the standard API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope and is the default when no scope is checked. The work package list endpoint is under /api/v3, so api_v3 is the grant to request. No narrower read-only scope is documented.
